summary: Feed 'one_way' to IDS is degraded: 40.0% of TCP sessions (80/200) are one-way, exceeding 10% threshold. IDS requires bidirectional traffic, so detection coverage is significantly reduced.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker/SPAN is forwarding only one direction for many flows - likely asymmetric routing with single-sided SPAN/TAP or broker hash/policy that splits client->server and server->client to different tool ports, so return traffic never reaches this IDS port.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs_both_directions=true for TCP reassembly, stream tracking and signature matching. With 40% one-way sessions it cannot reconstruct flows, causing missed intrusions, broken state tracking and high false-negative rate.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each session to the same IDS tool port using symmetric 5-tuple hashing so the IDS sees complete bidirectional flows required for stateful detection.
